author: Al Jazeera English
description:
In this week’s Inside Latin America is a Reporter’s Notebook from Lucia Newman on the ground in Colombia, following the aftermath of the quake and the efforts to reach survivors, deliver aid and clear rubble.  In affected areas, families are still searching for relatives, neighbours are helping each other, and emergency teams are working against time as the scale of the disaster becomes clearer.  The timing is politically significant. The earthquake came just days into President Abelardo de la Espriella’s presidency,  making it his first major national emergency and an early test of his government, coordination, response and public confidence.
 
This is a first-hand account of what the disaster looks and feels like on the ground — the rescue effort, the human toll, and the communities trying to rebuild after one of Colombia’s most serious emergencies in decades.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The Rohingya of Myanmar have faced decades of discrimination and forced displacement, and a case alleging genocide now sits before the International Court of Justice.

This film describes how military regimes rewrote citizenship laws to exclude Rohingya from registers and used identity documents, checkpoints and travel permits to control movement. It also highlights how segregation, incitement and continuing waves of violence normalised their erasure from the community.

Focusing on the 2016-2017 “clearance operations”, the film documents village burnings, mass killings and the flight of hundreds of thousands of Rohingya to Bangladesh. Through survivor testimony and interviews with officials and legal experts, Myanmar: The Architecture of Statelessness examines whether these crimes meet the legal threshold for genocide, how Myanmar defends itself against the allegation and what is ultimately at stake when the court delivers its verdict.

#myanmar #documentary #rohingya #documentary #a
title: How decades of persecution displaced Myanmar’s Rohingya | Al Jazeera Untangles

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Tens of thousands of mourners gathered in London to remember former Cambridge professor Jason Arday, whose supporters are demanding an inquiry into what they describe as a racist campaign against him. 
Arday, who became Cambridge's youngest Black professor in 2023, resigned on August 5 amid scrutiny over allegations of plagiarism and other claims. 
He denied the accusations but acknowledged making errors, while an investigation into his doctoral thesis at Liverpool John Moores University did not uphold a plagiarism complaint. 
Cambridge later opened an independent investigation into his appointment and academic work. 
Arday was found dead at his home nine days after resigning, with police saying his death was unexpected but not suspicious. 
His supporters say he faced sustained abuse and misinformation but claims that racism or media coverage contributed to his death have not been officially established. 

Al Jazeera's Sonia Gallego reports from London.

title: Thousands mourn Jason Arday in London, blaming ‘racist’ press for his death

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The US administration's latest diplomatic push on Gaza, led by Jared Kushner's meetings with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas, appears to have yielded no major breakthrough. 
Al Jazeera senior political analyst Marwan Bishara said Netanyahu will "give the appearance of getting along" with Kushner but "won't really go along with the plan" for Gaza. Bishara said Netanyahu's announcement of two committees to discuss the plan is a tactic to "bury the issue", noting that "when you want to bury an issue, make a committee for it." He said Netanyahu is "looking down the barrel" at a possible election loss in October, while Trump is also facing electoral pressures, so both leaders will "keep up the appearance" of negotiations without making "serious progress." Bishara said Israel has maintained "freedom of action" in Gaza and continues to occupy about half of the Strip. He also questioned how Hamas could be disarmed without Palestinian
title: Netanyahu gets along with Kushner to avoid going along with Gaza plan: Marwan Bishara
